\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{لوہا} (lohā)}{لوہا (lohā)}]{\ur{لوہا} (lohā) — iron}

\label{lesson:UR-C501-loha}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to darn, then the Urdu for to come unstitched.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{لوہا}}
\textbf{\ur{لوہا}} — \emph{lohā} — \textquotedblleft{}iron\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{لوہار} \ur{لوہے} \ur{سے} \ur{اوزار} \ur{بناتا} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{lohār lohe se auzār banātā hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The blacksmith makes tools out of iron.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{لوہا}} (\emph{lohā}) is inherited from Sanskrit \emph{lōha}, \textquotedblleft{}red, copper-coloured\textquotedblright{}, later \textquotedblleft{}copper\textquotedblright{} and \textquotedblleft{}iron\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 11158).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lohā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lohā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lohār lohe se auzār banātā hai.} — The blacksmith makes tools out of iron.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to darn, then the Urdu for to come unstitched, then say \emph{lohā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{لوہا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Iron\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{پیتل} (pītal)}{پیتل (pītal)}]{\ur{پیتل} (pītal) — brass}

\label{lesson:UR-C501-pital}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to come unstitched, then the Urdu for iron.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{پیتل}}
\textbf{\ur{پیتل}} — \emph{pītal} — \textquotedblleft{}brass\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{یہ} \ur{پرانا} \ur{برتن} \ur{پیتل} \ur{کا} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yih purānā bartan pītal kā hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This old pot is made of brass.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{پیتل}} (\emph{pītal}) is inherited from Sanskrit \emph{pittala}, \textquotedblleft{}brass\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 8184).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pītal}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{yih purānā bartan pītal kā hai.} — This old pot is made of brass.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to come unstitched, then the Urdu for iron, then say \emph{pītal} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{پیتل} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Brass\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{زیور} (zevar)}{زیور (zevar)}]{\ur{زیور} (zevar) — a piece of jewellery}

\label{lesson:UR-C501-zevar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for iron, then the Urdu for brass.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{زیور}}
\textbf{\ur{زیور}} — \emph{zevar} — \textquotedblleft{}a piece of jewellery\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{سنار} \ur{نے} \ur{دلہن} \ur{کے} \ur{لیے} \ur{زیور} \ur{بنائے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sunār ne dulhan ke liye zevar banāe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The goldsmith made jewellery for the bride.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{زیور}} (\emph{zevar}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{zēvar}, \textquotedblleft{}an ornament, jewellery\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{zevar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{zevar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sunār ne dulhan ke liye zevar banāe.} — The goldsmith made jewellery for the bride.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for iron, then the Urdu for brass, then say \emph{zevar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{زیور} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A piece of jewellery\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{پگھلانا} (pighlānā)}{پگھلانا (pighlānā)}]{\ur{پگھلانا} (pighlānā) — to melt (something)}

\label{lesson:UR-C501-pighlana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for brass, then the Urdu for jewellery.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{پگھلانا}}
\textbf{\ur{پگھلانا}} — \emph{pighlānā} — \textquotedblleft{}to melt (something)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{لوہار} \ur{نے} \ur{آگ} \ur{میں} \ur{لوہا} \ur{پگھلایا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{lohār ne āg meṅ lohā pighlāyā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The blacksmith melted the iron in the fire.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{پیتل} \ur{پگھلایا}, \emph{us ne pītal pighlāyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{پگھلانا}} (\emph{pighlānā}) is the causative of \emph{pighalnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to melt\textquotedblright{}, which CDIAL lists under \emph{*praghirati}, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 8486).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pighlānā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pighlānā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lohār ne āg meṅ lohā pighlāyā.} — The blacksmith melted the iron in the fire.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for brass, then the Urdu for jewellery, then say \emph{pighlānā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{پگھلانا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To melt (something)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{مڑھنا} (maṛhnā)}{مڑھنا (maṛhnā)}]{\ur{مڑھنا} (maṛhnā) — to plate (with metal); to encase}

\label{lesson:UR-C501-marhna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for jewellery, then the Urdu for to melt (something).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{مڑھنا}}
\textbf{\ur{مڑھنا}} — \emph{maṛhnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to plate (with metal); to encase\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{کاریگر} \ur{نے} \ur{تختے} \ur{پر} \ur{پیتل} \ur{مڑھا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kārīgar ne takhte par pītal maṛhā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The craftsman plated the board with brass.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{دروازے} \ur{پر} \ur{لوہا} \ur{مڑھا}, \emph{us ne darvāze par lohā maṛhā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{مڑھنا}} (\emph{maṛhnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{maṛhnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to cover, to overspread, to encrust\textquotedblright{}, under \emph{*maḍh}, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 9729).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{maṛhnā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{maṛhnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kārīgar ne takhte par pītal maṛhā.} — The craftsman plated the board with brass.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for jewellery, then the Urdu for to melt (something), then say \emph{maṛhnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{مڑھنا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To plate (with metal); to encase\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(dialogue)]{Looking back: from Looking for Work to Metal and Jewellery}

\label{lesson:UR-R501-review-494-501}



\begin{quote}
Say the Urdu for an interview (for a job) and employment.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item an interview (for a job), employment, a vacancy, dismissed from a job, to recruit
  \item wages, a strike, expertise, a contractor, to use up (time or effort)
  \item a workshop, a clamp, a hole, to bore (a hole), sandpaper
  \item a plank, sawdust, a carpenter's plane, to knock in, to file (metal or wood)
  \item a potter's wheel, a mould, a potter's kiln, a large clay pot, to heat in a fire
  \item cotton (the plant), to card (cotton), a spinning wheel, to spin (thread), a knot
  \item a sleeve, to have (clothes) sewn, to unpick (stitches), to darn, to come unstitched
  \item iron, brass, jewellery, to melt (something), to plate (with metal)
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
An interview (for a job)? (\textbf{\ur{انٹرویو}}, \emph{inṭarvyū}.) Employment? (\textbf{\ur{روزگار}}, \emph{rozgār}.) A vacancy? (\textbf{\ur{اسامی}}, \emph{asāmī}.) Dismissed from a job? (\textbf{\ur{برطرف}}, \emph{bartaraf}.) To recruit? (\textbf{\ur{بھرتی} \ur{کرنا}}, \emph{bhartī karnā}.) Wages? (\textbf{\ur{اجرت}}, \emph{ujrat}.) A strike? (\textbf{\ur{ہڑتال}}, \emph{haṛtāl}.) Expertise? (\textbf{\ur{مہارت}}, \emph{mahārat}.) A contractor? (\textbf{\ur{ٹھیکیدار}}, \emph{ṭhekedār}.) To use up (time or effort)? (\textbf{\ur{کھپانا}}, \emph{khapānā}.) A workshop? (\textbf{\ur{ورکشاپ}}, \emph{varkshāp}.) A clamp? (\textbf{\ur{شکنجہ}}, \emph{shikanjā}.) A hole? (\textbf{\ur{سوراخ}}, \emph{surākh}.) To bore (a hole)? (\textbf{\ur{چھیدنا}}, \emph{chhednā}.) Sandpaper? (\textbf{\ur{ریگمال}}, \emph{regmāl}.) A plank? (\textbf{\ur{تختہ}}, \emph{takhtā}.) Sawdust? (\textbf{\ur{برادہ}}, \emph{burādā}.) A carpenter's plane? (\textbf{\ur{رندا}}, \emph{randā}.) To knock in? (\textbf{\ur{ٹھونکنا}}, \emph{ṭhoṅknā}.) To file (metal or wood)? (\textbf{\ur{ریتنا}}, \emph{retnā}.) A potter's wheel? (\textbf{\ur{چاک}}, \emph{chāk}.) A mould? (\textbf{\ur{سانچا}}, \emph{sāṅchā}.) A potter's kiln? (\textbf{\ur{آوا}}, \emph{āvā}.) A large clay pot? (\textbf{\ur{مٹکا}}, \emph{maṭkā}.) To heat in a fire? (\textbf{\ur{تپانا}}, \emph{tapānā}.) Cotton (the plant)? (\textbf{\ur{کپاس}}, \emph{kapās}.) To card (cotton)? (\textbf{\ur{دھننا}}, \emph{dhunnā}.) A spinning wheel? (\textbf{\ur{چرخہ}}, \emph{charkhā}.) To spin (thread)? (\textbf{\ur{کاتنا}}, \emph{kātnā}.) A knot? (\textbf{\ur{گانٹھ}}, \emph{gāṅṭh}.) A sleeve? (\textbf{\ur{آستین}}, \emph{āstīn}.) To have (clothes) sewn? (\textbf{\ur{سلوانا}}, \emph{silvānā}.) To unpick (stitches)? (\textbf{\ur{ادھیڑنا}}, \emph{udheṛnā}.) To darn? (\textbf{\ur{رفو} \ur{کرنا}}, \emph{rafū karnā}.) To come unstitched? (\textbf{\ur{ادھڑنا}}, \emph{udhaṛnā}.) Iron? (\textbf{\ur{لوہا}}, \emph{lohā}.) Brass? (\textbf{\ur{پیتل}}, \emph{pītal}.) Jewellery? (\textbf{\ur{زیور}}, \emph{zevar}.) To melt (something)? (\textbf{\ur{پگھلانا}}, \emph{pighlānā}.) To plate (with metal)? (\textbf{\ur{مڑھنا}}, \emph{maṛhnā}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
